visual_context_notes.observation: The first sampled slide asks "Is OneCoin A SCAM?!?!?!" above a coin-like OneCoin image.
A Forbes BrandVoice page is shown with text saying BrandVoice offers credible voices that are "always transparently identified" and helps fund independent journalism.

A later slide about the Forbes Bulgaria interview says Facebook followers had raised speculations and that OneCoin wanted to clarify them; it states that BrandVoice content is paid advertising content and Forbes Bulgaria does not represent the product or service by using the same tools journalists use.

A coinmarket-capitalization page and a marked-up OneCoin market capitalization slide are shown, including text saying OneCoin is a new cryptocurrency and that only the ONE Network can mine and trade the coin at the ONE Exchange.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes paid OneCoin-related packages linked to tokens for mining, registration fees, card access to claimed earnings, and listed euro prices. It also claims 285 newly created millionaires and prompts membership as a life-changing opportunity, going beyond neutral discussion. Forbes-related material is shown, but the disclosure identifies it as paid advertising and says Forbes Bulgaria does not represent the product, while the wealth, token, earnings, and gold-related claims are not verified.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: Paid package participation is explicitly linked to tokens and a mining process, with the presentation also describing access to claimed earnings through OnePay. The evidence supports a paid mining-related package mechanism, although it does not establish that mining or earnings actually occurred.
